intent: Extract a transparent production otter head and thin waterline ripples from the user-approved smiling-head preview

prompt:
Use case: background-extraction / precise-object-edit. Production raster layer for the user-approved website preview. Image 1 is the approved desktop-left/mobile-right board. EXTRACT ONLY the LARGE SMILING OTTER HEAD from the DESKTOP panel and its very close thin waterline ripples into ONE isolated transparent-background asset. Image 2, the existing whale, is a style reference only. Preserve the approved otter's exact character, gentle closed-mouth smile, softly squinting happy eyes, lifted cheek pads, nose/ear/whisker shapes, gaze and head orientation. Do not redesign the face or change its proportions. Preserve the defined ink-blue contours, grouped navy/slate painted fur planes and sparse cool ivory highlights. It must look like the same approved head, not a new cartoon or photo.
ONLY HEAD visible; head base ends at a natural waterline directly below the jaw. NO shell, objects, paws, knuckles, arms, shoulders, chest, torso, feet or tail. Its entire body is submerged and invisible. Include only a FEW THIN broken navy/slate/silver ripple curves closely surrounding the head base, with one or two thin foreground strokes crossing the lowest fur to establish immersion. Do not include any large filled water surface, rectangular backdrop, sky, scenery, UI, type, gutter, control or other animals. Ripple center and waterline belong near the lower quarter of the image.
Make a WIDE 2:1 canvas with genuine transparent alpha. Center the head horizontally; head occupies about 60% of image width and 70% of image height. The widest thin ripple may occupy 90% of width. Keep at least5% clear transparent padding on EVERY edge around head, whiskers and ripples. All pixels outside the actual head silhouette and those sparse thin ripple strokes must be fully transparent alpha. No checkerboard, solid blue plane, white matte, shadow or halo. Background removal must not erase fine whiskers or replace the smiling face. This is ONE production cutout, not another preview board. Keep precisely the approved smile.
